title: Canonical Zariski-etale module functor square and flat-base-change section maps
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its Zariski site [def-sc-zariski-site] and small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and put $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}(v:V\to T)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. Write $L_T=\epsilon_T^*$ for tensor pullback and $R_T=\epsilon_{T,*}$ for restriction to open subschemes along the canonical morphism of ringed sites $\epsilon_T:T_{\mathrm{et}}\to T_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ [lem-trf-zariski-etale-tensor-sections]. Modules mean sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; Zariski quasi-coherence is [pqf-def-coherent] and site quasi-coherence is [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $a:U\to T$ be any scheme morphism. Write $a^*$ for scheme tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], and $a_{\mathrm{et}}^*,a_{\mathrm{et},*}$ for tensor pullback and direct image on ringed small etale topoi [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. For every etale module $G$ on $U$, there is a canonical natural identification $R_Ta_{\mathrm{et},*}G\simeq a_*R_UG$, equal on an open $W\subseteq T$ to the identity of $G(a^{-1}W\hookrightarrow U)$ with its prescribed scalar action. Its adjoint comparison is a natural isomorphism $L_Ua^*M\simeq a_{\mathrm{et}}^*L_TM$ for every Zariski module $M$, without a quasi-coherence hypothesis; the comparison is the one determined by the specified module adjunctions and their units and counits. Suppose further that $a$ is quasi-compact and separated [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local], and $H$ is a quasi-coherent Zariski module on $U$. Then $a_*H$ is quasi-coherent. For each etale $v:V\to T$, put $U_V=U\times_TV$, with projections $a_V:U_V\to V$ and $v':U_V\to U$. The canonical degree-zero flat base-change map $v^*a_*H\to a_{V,*}v'^*H$ is an isomorphism. The resulting maps $\Gamma(V,v^*a_*H)\to\Gamma(U_V,v'^*H)$ are natural in $V,H$, are the section maps of a canonical isomorphism $L_T(a_*H)\simeq a_{\mathrm{et},*}L_UH$, and on an open $V=W\subseteq T$ are the identity of $\Gamma(a^{-1}W,H)$.

source.place: Tags 03FH (remark-change-topologies-ringed-sites), part (2), and 03LC (proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial), parts (1),(3): canonical adjunction square and degree-zero flat-base-change section comparison.

proof.text: Obtain c and the normalized section family e from [lem-trf-etale-extension-free-presentations-hom]. Its linearity, module naturality and open-unit clauses are exactly the first three requested equations. Ignore its additional free-presentation and localization clauses.

Apply [lem-trf-zariski-etale-right-adjoint-square] to a,cU,cT. It supplies hp and r with the exact open-coordinate normalization. The specified pullback comparison is already a natural isomorphism by its conjugateIsoEquiv definition, so every component is invertible.

For quasi-compact separated a, use [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] (separated implies quasi-separated) to get the quasi-coherent direct image. For an etale test V choose injective resolutions of H and of its pullback to V×_T U. Both vertical etale maps are flat. The augmented lift of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-lift] gives t. The resolution comparison is invertible by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-resolution-iso]. In degree zero [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-resolution-degree-zero] identifies its composite with the canonical moduleBaseChangeMap followed by the zeroth-derived-functor identification. Cancel that identification to prove the actual moduleBaseChangeMap invertible.

Apply [lem-trf-zariski-etale-pushforward-section-formula] with c,e and the three normalization equations, plus hp,r and its open formula. This supplies the required equality with the actual moduleBaseChangeMap on top sections. Its right side is invertible by step 3; cancel the two e-components to make every additive section component of the small-etale pushforward comparison invertible. Objectwise invertibility makes its underlying presheaf map invertible, and the forgetful functors from sheaves and from module sheaves reflect isomorphisms. Thus the comparison itself is invertible.

Naturality holds on all modules: compose the small-etale pullback unit, the inverse pullback-comparison transformation, and extension of the scheme pullback counit, and take its naturality equation. For the final unit identity, apply unit_conjugateEquiv_symm to the composite scheme/extension and extension/small-etale adjunctions with r.inv. Expand the composite units, compose with the extension of the scheme counit, and cancel r.inv against r.hom by naturality. Naturality of the extension unit and the right triangle identity of scheme pullback/pushforward give exactly pushforward of the extension unit. No quasi-coherence is needed for either formal identity.
